workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§214–217
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§214–217: Boroqul, Usun and Quildar
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§214–217, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Chinggis Qahan continues the rewards of 1206. He tells Boroqul how his mother reared four boys as companions for her sons, and how Boroqul's wife Altani, with Jetei and Jelme, saved the boy Tolui from the Tatar Qargil-Shira, and how Boroqul sucked the clotted blood from the wounded Ögödei and brought him back alive; for this Boroqul is told that he is not to be penalised if he incurs a penalty nine times. A one-line favour for a girl's kin follows (§215). Usun-Ebügen is made beki, to be robed in white and set on a white gelding (§216), and Quildar's descendants are granted a grant because he put his life at risk in battle and was first to open his mouth (§217).
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Boroγul-a ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, to Boroγul saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Boroqul:
sentences.n: The colon opens Chinggis's speech to Boroqul. It is one long speech: Shiratori's opening quotation mark comes at Eke (unit 2) and the closing mark at aldatuγai (unit 49), and it contains three smaller speeches that Shiratori does not mark; in `i` I mark those with single quotes. Boroγul-a is a name with the dative-locative -a (Ming 行), 'to'. ügülerün is ügüle- 'to speak' with the time converb -rün, 'when saying', used simply to bring in speech. Čiṅgis is the title, printed with the dotted ṅ.

sentences.t: "Eke min-u Šigi-Qutuqu, Boroγul, Küčü, Kököčü ta dörben-(n)i

morph.gloss: genitive: my, set after its noun
accusative: marks the object (the (n) is Shiratori's)

sentences.l: "Mother my, Šigi-Qutuqu, Boroγul, Küčü, Kököčü, you four-(acc)
sentences.i: “My mother, you four, Shigi-Qutuqu, Boroqul, Küchü and Kököchü,
sentences.n: A sentence begins that runs through unit 7 and ends in težiġebe-že, 'reared (you), indeed'. Read min-u as 'my', set after its noun (Eke min-u, 'mother my'; min-u is the genitive of bi 'I'); the mother is presumably Högelün, though the text does not name her here. The four names stand in apposition to ta dörben-(n)i, 'you four', with the accusative -(n)i (the (n) is Shiratori's); ta is plural 'you' (Ming 您), so Chinggis is speaking to the four of them, Boroqul by name. The verbs come in the next unit (olžu 'getting') and in unit 7 (težiġe- 'to rear'), so `i` supplies none here and carries 'you four' over to them. The opening quotation mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: irgen-ü nutuγ-ača köser-eče olžu köl- dür(i)-jen dürüžü

morph.gloss: ground, earth (stem read from the Ming) [地行]
foot (first half of a word broken at the line end: köl-dür(i)-jen) [腳]
to cast, throw, take in (stem inferred from the Ming 投; uncertain) [投着]

sentences.l: people's camp-from, ground-from getting, foot-at-own casting,
sentences.i: getting you from the people's camp, from the ground, and taking you in at her own feet,
sentences.n: A converb chain: olžu (ol- 'to get, find' + -žu, '…ing'; Ming 得着 'getting') and dürüžü ('…ing'). nutuγ-ača and köser-eče are ablatives, 'from the camp', 'from the ground' (the Ming gives 行 for both, as it often does for -ača/-eče; I follow the form, so `i` says 'from', not 'in'). köl- and dür(i)-jen are one word broken at the line end: köl-dür-jen, 'at one's own foot', with the dative-locative -dür and the reflexive-possessive -jen (the (i) is Shiratori's). dürüžü is a guess at the stem: the Ming 投 'throw, cast' can also mean 'take refuge with', so 'taking you in' is tentative; 'at her own feet' may be a figure for 'under her care'.

sentences.t: köġüčilen asaražu težiġerün

morph.gloss: to lift up, raise (stem inferred from the Ming) [擡擧着]

sentences.l: son-as lifting, rearing-when,
sentences.i: raising you as her sons, and while she reared you,
sentences.n: köġüčilen is köġü 'son' plus -čilen, 'as a son' (the Ming 做兒子); I take the ending to be -čila- 'make into' with the converb -n, but that is a guess. asara- 'to lift up' is inferred from the Ming 擡擧. težiġerün is težiġe- 'to rear' with the time converb -rün, 'while rearing'. The chain goes on: -žu 'and then', -rün 'while'.

sentences.t: küžüġün-eče tan-u tatažu küġün-lüġe sačaγ̇un bolγažu
sentences.l: neck-from your pulling, man-with equal making,
sentences.i: lifting you up by the neck and making you the equals of people,
sentences.n: Ming 項頸行 for küžüġün-eče: 'neck', with the Ming's usual 行 although the form is the ablative 'from'. tan-u is the genitive of ta ('of you', Ming 您的), standing where an accusative 'you' would be natural; I take it as 'you'. tatažu is tata- 'to pull' (the Ming 提 'lift'); to lift a child by the neck, and (next unit) the shoulder, is an image of bringing him up to man's estate, which is my reading, not the glossators'. küġün is 'man, person' (Ming 人), so `i` says 'people' here and 'men' for ere in the next unit. sačaγ̇un: the Ming 齊每 'all alike'. bolγažu is bol- 'become' with the causative -γa- and -žu, 'making (them) become'.

sentences.t: egemēče tan-u tatažu ere-lüġe sačaγ̇u bolγažu

morph.gloss: shoulder (stem inferred from the Ming 肩甲) [肩甲行]
ablative: from (written with a long vowel)

sentences.l: shoulder-from your pulling, male-with equal making,
sentences.i: lifting you up by the shoulder and making you the equals of men,
sentences.n: The same pattern as the previous unit. egemēče is egem 'shoulder' (inferred from the Ming 肩甲 'shoulder-blade') with the ablative written with a long vowel; ere is 'man, male' (Ming 男子). The Ming 敎做者︀ at the end shows it takes bolγažu as causative.

sentences.t: köġüd-ü-ġen man-a nökör seġüder bolγsau keġen težiġebe-že.

morph.gloss: linking vowel before the reflexive-possessive after the plural -d (not a genitive)
we, exclusive (oblique stem man-; Ming 俺) [俺行]
converb that closes a quotation: saying

sentences.l: sons-their-own, to-us companion, shadow let-be-made, saying, reared-indeed.
sentences.i: intending that you should be companions and a shadow to us, her own sons, she reared you.
sentences.n: The main verb at last: težiġebe-že (težiġe- 'to rear', past -be, assertion particle -že, 'indeed'). I read köġüd-ü-ġen man-a as 'to us, her own sons': köġüd is 'sons' with the reflexive-possessive -ġen, and man-a is ba 'we' (exclusive, the oblique stem man-; the Ming 俺, against 咱 for the inclusive bida) with the dative -a (Ming 俺行). bolγsau is 'let (them) be made' (a variant optative; uncertain). keġen 'saying' closes a thought, so `i` gives it as 'intending'. Whether 'sons' means Chinggis and his brothers or his own children is not settled by the words; the Ming 兒子每自的 'her own sons' fits the former.

sentences.t: Tan-i težiġegsen hači-ban eke-de maqa min-u kedüi hači tusa qariγ̇lba ta.

morph.gloss: you (plural, polite; stem tan- before a case ending) [您行]
-gsen = past participle: 'that has reared' (here 'the having reared')
genitive: my, set after its noun
to repay, requite (stem inferred from the Ming; compare qari- 'return') [囘報了]

sentences.l: You-acc reared requital-own mother-to, perhaps my how-much requital favour repaid you.
sentences.i: For the rearing of you, how much, I wonder, have you repaid my mother in requital of her favour?
sentences.n: A hard sentence, and the translation is a best reading. Tan-i težiġegsen is 'the having reared you' (past participle, accusative); hači-ban 'its own requital' (Ming 囘報, 'repayment'); eke-de 'to the mother'. maqa is 'perhaps' (Ming 莫); kedüi 'how much'. min-u, 'my', again stands after its noun, and here I attach it loosely to eke 'mother'. qariγ̇lba is qariγ̇l- 'to repay', the stem inferred from the Ming 囘報. I take the sentence as a question that praises (the following units list what they did), but the tone is not marked.

sentences.t: Boroγul na-dur nököčeldüžü qurdun ajan-dur qura süni qoγ̇osun ese qonoγ̇ulba-že či.

morph.gloss: campaign, march out (Ming 出征) [出征 裏]
rain (the Ming brackets 雨, i.e. supplied) [(雨)]
to pass the night [敎宿了 也者︀]

sentences.l: Boroγul, me-to companion-being, swiftly campaign-in, rain night empty, not-yet made-pass-the-night-indeed you.
sentences.i: Boroqul, you, as my companion, never let me pass a night empty in the rain on swift campaigns.
sentences.n: Chinggis turns to Boroqul alone. nököčeldüžü is nököče- 'to be a companion', -ldü- 'together', -žü '…ing'. ese … qonoγ̇ulba-že is 'did not make (me) pass the night' (ese 'not' of a past act; qono- 'to pass the night' + causative + past + -že). The Ming brackets 雨 'rain' as supplied. qoγ̇osun 'empty' (Ming 空): empty of what is not said; I have left it as 'empty', which may mean 'without shelter' or 'for nothing'. The period after či ends the first of two parallel sentences.

sentences.t: šitüġeleldüžü büküi daisun-dur sülen ügei ese qonoγ̇ulba-že či

morph.gloss: to resist, oppose (stem inferred from the Ming 抗拒) [相抗拒着]
to pass the night [敎宿了 也者︀]

sentences.l: resisting-one-another being enemies-against, soup without, not-yet made-pass-the-night-indeed you
sentences.i: And when we stood in resistance against the enemy, you never let me pass the night without broth.
sentences.n: The second half of the parallel: šitüġeleldüžü is šitüġe- 'to resist' (Ming 抗拒), reciprocal -leldü-, -žü; büküi daisun-dur is 'being, against the enemy'; daisun is singular, so `i` says 'the enemy'. sülen is 'soup, broth' (Ming 湯); sülen ügei, 'without soup', I take to mean a hot meal, but a figurative sense is possible. The unit has no full stop at its end in Shiratori.

sentences.t: Basa ebüges ečige-ji baraγsad öšiten kišiten Tatar irgen-i doraidaγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: to be finished, ruined [了了的每]
feud, grudge (read from the Ming 讐) [讐有的每]
grievance, wrong (stem inferred from the Ming 寃) [寃有的每]
to subdue, crush (stem inferred from the Ming 壓服) [壓服下了着]

sentences.l: Again forefathers father-acc ruined-those, feud-having, grievance-having Tatar people-acc subduing,
sentences.i: Again, having subdued the Tatar people, who had ruined the forefathers and the father, with whom there was feud and grievance,
sentences.n: baraγsad is bara- 'to be finished, ruined' with the plural past participle -γsad, 'those who ruined'; ebüges ečige-ji, 'forefathers (plural -s) (and) father (accusative)'. öšiten and kišiten are noun + the possessive plural -ten, 'those having a feud, those having a grievance' (the Ming 讐有的每, 寃有的每), which `i` keeps as 'with whom there was feud and grievance'; the stems öši and kiši are read from the Ming. doraidaγ̇ulžu: doraida- 'to subdue', stem inferred from 壓服 'press down'; with -γ̇ul- causative.

sentences.t: ösül ösen kisal kisan

morph.gloss: to avenge, requite (stem inferred from kisal and the Ming) [報]

sentences.l: enmity avenging, grievance avenging
sentences.i: taking vengeance for the enmity and requital for the wrong,
sentences.n: Paired cognates, a Mongol habit: ösül ösen (ösül 'enmity', Ming 讐; ösen the verb, 'repaying', Ming 報) and kisal kisan (kisal 'grievance', Ming 寃; kisan the verb, 'avenging', Ming 報). The verb stems are guesses from the nouns and the Ming 報, and the final -n of each is either a converb or a participle ending.

sentences.t: Tatar irgen-i čiγ̇un-dur uližu ülidgen kiduqui-dur alaγdarun

morph.gloss: linchpin of a cart [車轄 裏]
utterly, completely (the Ming 盡絕 'wholly cut off'; stem uncertain) [盡絕]

sentences.l: Tatar people-acc linchpin-at measuring, utterly destroying-at-the-time, being-killed-when
sentences.i: when the Tatar people were measured against the linchpin of a cart, at the time of their utter destruction, when they were being killed,
sentences.n: čiγ̇un-dur uližu is 'at the linchpin, measuring' (čiγ̇un 'linchpin', Ming 車轄; uli- 'to compare', Ming 比). The Ming gives only 'compare with the linchpin'; it is a measure by which the people were judged, presumably by height, but the words do not say, and I add nothing. kiduqui-dur is kidu- 'to destroy utterly' with the participle -qui and -dur, 'at the time of'; alaγdarun is ala- 'to kill', passive -γda-, converb -run, 'when killed'. kiduqui-dur is active ('at the time of destroying') with the Tatars as its object; `i` gives 'their destruction' and names no one. ülidgen, Ming 盡絕 'wholly cut off', I take as 'utterly'; the stem is uncertain.

sentences.t: Tatar-un Qargil-Šira oγ̇určaγ bolun γarču žiči jadažu ölöčü orožu irežü

words.reading: 中合舌兒吉勒-失舌剌 Qargil-Šira

morph.gloss: Qargil-Shira, a man's name (a Tatar) [(人)名]
to be hungry (stem inferred from the Ming 饑) [饑着]

sentences.l: Tatars' Qargil-Šira brigand becoming, going-out, but, being-in-want, being-hungry, entering, coming,
sentences.i: Qargil-Shira of the Tatars, who had become a brigand and gone out, but was destitute and starving, and came in,
sentences.n: The story inside the speech begins. The man's name is printed Qargil-Šira here and Γargil-Šira from unit 19 on; they are the same man, and `i` writes Qargil-Shira throughout. oγ̇určaγ bolun is 'becoming a robber' (Ming 劫賊 做). žiči jadažu ölöčü is 'but, being in want, being hungry' (žiči 'but', Ming 郤); ölö- 'to be hungry' is the stem inferred from the Ming 饑. A converb chain, each -žu/-žü/-čü 'and then'.

sentences.t: eke-dür ger-te orožu sai eriġülšün bijü bi keġežü

morph.gloss: ending of one who seeks (uncertain; Ming 尋的)

sentences.l: mother-at tent-in entering, good seeking is, I, saying,
sentences.i: he entered my mother's tent, saying, ‘I am one who seeks what is good,’
sentences.n: eke-dür ger-te is 'at the mother, in the tent'. Shiratori marks no quotation here, so the quotation marks in `i` are mine. sai eriġülšün bijü bi is 'a seeker of good (Ming 好 尋的) there is, I'. What 'good' means is not said: a good place, a good man, kindness; I keep the neutral 'what is good'. The ending -ġülšün is not explained; the stem is eri- 'to seek'.

sentences.t: sai eriġülšün böġesü tende saγ̇u keġegdežü

morph.gloss: ending of one who seeks (uncertain; Ming 尋的)

sentences.l: good seeking if-be, there sit, being-told,
sentences.i: ‘If you seek what is good, sit there,’ he was told,
sentences.n: böġesü is the conditional of bü- 'to be', 'if it be that'. saγ̇u is the bare stem of saγ̇u- 'to sit', used as an imperative (Ming 坐). keġegdežü is keġe- 'to say' with the passive -gde- and -žü, 'being told' (Ming 被說着); who told him is not stated, presumably the mother. Shiratori marks no quotation here either; the single quotes in `i` are mine.

sentences.t: höreneži iseri-jin alaγun-a üžeġür-e saγ̇užu büküi-dür

morph.gloss: place behind the door (Ming 門後; stem uncertain) [門後行]

sentences.l: west-side bed's behind-door at tip-at sitting being-when,
sentences.i: and while he sat on the west side, behind the door at the end of the bed,
sentences.n: höreneži 'on the west side' (hörene 'west', reading uncertain; -ži 'toward'). iseri-jin alaγun-a üžeġür-e: 'of the bed, behind the door, at the tip', which I read as 'at the end of the bed, behind the door'; the Ming (床的 門後行 捎頭行) does not fix which noun governs which. büküi-dür is the participle 'being' plus dative-locative, 'at the time of being', 'while'.

sentences.t: Tului tabun nasutu γadanača orožu irežü žiči güjižü γarču odun büküi-ji

morph.gloss: Tolui, a boy's name (printed Tului; Chinggis's son) [(兒)名]
outside (stem read from the Ming 自外) [自外]

sentences.l: Tului, five years-having, from-outside entering coming, but running going-out going being-acc,
sentences.i: Tolui, who was five years old, came in from outside, but ran out; as he was going,
sentences.n: nasutu is nasu 'age, years' with the possessive -tu, 'having years', so 'aged five' (Ming 五 歲有的). γadanača is 'from outside' (γadana from the Ming 自外, ablative -ča). žiči is "but, yet", given as "but". The unit ends in büküi-ji, the participle 'being' with the accusative -ji: 'the (boy) who was going', set up as the object of the next unit's action.

sentences.t: Γargil-Šira bosuγ̇ad köġüken-i suγ̇u-dur(i)-jan qabčižu γarču jabužu

words.reading: 中合舌兒吉勒-失舌剌 Γargil-Šira

morph.gloss: Qargil-Shira, a man's name (printed here with Γ, the same man) [(人)名]
armpit (stem inferred from the Ming 肘腋) [肘腋 裏自的行]
to clamp, press (stem inferred from the Ming 夾) [夾着]

sentences.l: Γargil-Šira, rising, little-child-acc armpit-at-own clamping, going-out, going-about,
sentences.i: Qargil-Shira stood up, clamped the little boy under his own arm, and went out walking,
sentences.n: köġüken-i is köġü 'child' with the diminutive -ken and the accusative, 'the little child' (Ming 兒子 行). suγ̇u-dur(i)-jan is suγ̇u 'armpit' (Ming 肘腋, stem inferred) with -dur and the reflexive -(i)jan, 'in his own armpit'. qabčižu 'clamping', qabči- inferred from the Ming 夾. A converb chain: bosuγ̇ad, qabčižu, γarču, jabužu.

sentences.t: aisurun kituγai-ban temtelžü žuγulun jabuqui-dur

morph.gloss: to whet, rub (stem inferred from the Ming 磨) [磨着]
to draw out, pull out (stem inferred from the Ming 抽) [抽]

sentences.l: coming-when, knife-own whetting, drawing, going-about-at-the-time,
sentences.i: and as he came and went, whetting and drawing his knife,
sentences.n: aisurun is aisu- 'to come' with the time converb -run, 'when coming'; it sits oddly after jabužu 'going' and I read the two as 'going (to and fro) and coming'. temtelžü žuγulun: temtel- 'to whet, rub' (stem inferred from the Ming 磨 'grind') and žuγul- 'to draw out' (from the Ming 抽); 'whetting' may mean rubbing the blade to draw it. jabuqui-dur is the participle plus -dur, 'at the time of going about'. The sentence is still without a main verb.

sentences.t: Boroγul-un gergei Altani eke-jin ger-tür dorona saγ̇užu büleġe.

morph.gloss: east, on the east side [東行]

sentences.l: Boroγul's wife Altani, mother's tent-at east sitting, was.
sentences.i: Boroqul's wife Altani was sitting on the east side in my mother's tent.
sentences.n: The main clause of the long sentence: saγ̇užu büleġe, 'sitting was', converb + past of bü- 'to be', a past continuous. Altani is Boroqul's wife (Boroγul-un gergei, 'Boroqul's wife', genitive before its noun). ger-tür is ger 'tent' with -tür (front-vowel dative-locative); dorona is 'east, on the east side' (Ming 東行).

sentences.t: Eke qailažu köġün baraba keġeküi-lüġe

morph.gloss: to call out, cry out [叫着]
comitative: 'together with the saying', i.e. at the very moment

sentences.l: Mother, calling-out, son is-ruined saying-at-the-very-time,
sentences.i: My mother cried out that the boy was lost, and at that very moment,
sentences.n: Shiratori marks no quotation, so `i` reports the cry indirectly. köġün baraba is 'the son is finished, ruined' (bara- with the past -ba; Ming 了了 'finished'; the Mongol has no 'her', so `i` adds none), and has the sense 'the boy is lost'. keġeküi-lüġe is keġe- 'to say' with the participle -küi and the comitative -lüġe, 'together with the saying', i.e. as she said it (Ming 纔說間). The mother (Eke) is presumably the same Högelün.

sentences.t: Altani udaγ̇araldun güjižü γarulčažu

morph.gloss: to follow (stem inferred from the Ming 隨) [共隨卽]

sentences.l: Altani, following-together, running, going-out-together,
sentences.i: Altani ran out with her, close behind,
sentences.n: udaγ̇araldun (Ming 共隨卽 'following together') is a verb I read as udaγ̇ar- 'to follow' with the joint-action -ldu- and the converb -n; the stem is inferred from the Ming. γarulčažu 'going out together' (Ming 共出着): -ulča- is my guess for the joint-action ending. 'With her' in `i` is supplied; the Ming gives only 'together'.

sentences.t: Γargil-Šira-jin qoināča güjičežü šibilger in-ü barižu

words.reading: 中合舌兒吉勒-失舌剌-因 Γargil-Šira-jin

glyphs.s: 中合舌兒吉勒-失舌剌-因

morph.gloss: Qargil-Shira, a man's name (printed with Γ) [(人)名的]
to overtake, catch up (stem inferred from the Ming 趕上) [趕上着]
probably a braid or lock of hair (the Ming 練︀推 gives no sense; context only; uncertain) [練︀推]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to take hold of, grasp [拿着]

sentences.l: Γargil-Šira's from-behind overtaking, braid his seizing,
sentences.i: she overtook Qargil-Shira from behind and seized his braid,
sentences.n: qoināča is 'from behind' (qoina 'behind', short ablative -ča; Ming 後 行). güjičežü is güjiče- 'to overtake' (the Ming 趕上, stem inferred). Important: šibilger gets the Ming 練︀推, which is merely a transcription and gives no sense; 'braid' (or lock of hair) is a guess from the context, as she is seizing him from behind. in-ü 'his' follows its noun, like min-u; it repeats the genitive Γargil-Šira-jin.

sentences.t: nögöġe γar(i)-jar(i)-jan kituγai žuγulun büküi γar in-ü barižu tataqui-luγ̇a kituγai-ban aldažuγ̇ui.

words.reading: 中合舌里-牙舌里-顏 γar(i)-jar(i)-jan

morph.gloss: instrumental: with (the (i) before it is Shiratori's)
to draw out, pull out (stem inferred from the Ming 抽) [抽]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to take hold of, grasp [拿着]
to slip away, lose [脫了有來]

sentences.l: other hand-with-own, knife drawing being hand his seizing, pulling-while, knife-own slipped-away.
sentences.i: With her own other hand she seized the hand in which he was drawing the knife, and as she pulled, the knife slipped from his grip.
sentences.n: γar(i)-jar(i)-jan is γar 'hand' with the instrumental -jar and the reflexive -(i)jan, 'with her own hand'; nögöġe 'the other' (Ming 那箇) goes with it. büküi after the participle žuγulun 'drawing' makes 'the (hand) that was drawing', which is why γar in-ü, 'hand his', comes after it. tataqui-luγ̇a is tata- 'to pull' with the participle -qui and -luγ̇a, 'together with the pulling', 'while' (Ming 扯有間). aldažuγ̇ui is alda- 'to slip away' with the past -žuγ̇ui (uncertain; Ming 脫了有來).

sentences.t: Ger-ün ümere Žetei, Želme qojar Muqular qara hüker želen alažu büküi-dür

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form after a consonant)
food, something prepared to eat (Ming 做喫的; uncertain) [做喫的]

sentences.l: tent's north-at Jetei, Jelme two, hornless black ox food killing being-when,
sentences.i: North of the tent, Jetei and Jelme, the two of them, were slaughtering a hornless black ox for food,
sentences.n: Ger-ün ümere: 'of the tent, in the north' (ger-ün genitive, ümere 'north', Ming 北行). Žetei, Želme qojar, 'Jetei, Jelme, the two' with the number after the pair it counts. Muqular is 'hornless' (Ming 禿角) though printed with a capital; I take it as an adjective, not a name. želen (Ming 做喫的 'something made to eat') I read as 'for food'; uncertain. büküi-dür as before, 'while being'.

sentences.t: Altani-jin daγ̇un-dur Žetei, Želme qojar süke barižu nudurγaši-jan hulaγ̇adažu güjižü irežü

morph.gloss: Altani, a woman's name [(婦人)名的]
to take hold of, grasp [拿着]

words.reading: 訥都︀舌兒中合失-顏 nudurγaši-jan

morph.gloss: fist (Ming 拳頭) [拳頭 自的行]
to redden, be red (stem inferred from the Ming 紅) [紅着]

sentences.l: Altani's voice-at, Jetei, Jelme two, axe seizing, fist-own reddening, running, coming
sentences.i: at Altani's cry, Jetei and Jelme, the two of them, seized axes and came running, their fists red,
sentences.n: daγ̇un-dur is 'at the voice' (Ming 聲裏). nudurγaši-jan is 'their own fist(s)' (Ming 拳頭 自的行); hulaγ̇adažu is 'reddening' (stem inferred from the Ming 紅着), and I take the red to be the blood of the ox they were killing; the text does not say. süke is 'axe' (Ming 斧子), here singular in form, 'taking an axe each' is the sense. The Ming's 自的 shows -jan.

sentences.t: Tatar-un Γargil-Šira-ji süke-ber kituγai-bar mün tende alažuγ̇ui.

words.reading: 中合舌兒吉勒-失舌剌-冝 Γargil-Šira-ji

glyphs.s: 中合舌兒吉勒-失舌剌-冝

morph.gloss: Qargil-Shira, a man's name (printed with Γ) [人名行]
instrumental: with (back-vowel form after a vowel)

sentences.l: Tatars' Γargil-Šira-acc axe-with, knife-with, just there killed.
sentences.i: and killed Qargil-Shira of the Tatars on the spot, with axe and knife.
sentences.n: Tatar-un Γargil-Šira-ji is 'Qargil-Shira of the Tatars' in the accusative. süke-ber, kituγai-bar: the instrumental -ber/-bar, vowel-harmonised (front for süke, back for kituγai; Ming 斧子敎, 刀子敎). mün tende is 'just there' (Ming 只 那裏). alažuγ̇ui is the past of ala- 'to kill', the same ending as in aldažuγ̇ui (unit 25).

sentences.t: Altani, Žetei, Želme γurban köġün-ü amin aburaγsan žuldu temečeldüġešü

morph.gloss: to rescue, save (stem inferred from the Ming 救) [救了的]
first credit, foremost merit (Ming 頭功) [頭功]
to contend, vie (stem inferred from the Ming 爭) [相爭呵]

sentences.l: Altani, Jetei, Jelme three son's life rescued first-credit, contending-if,
sentences.i: When the three, Altani, Jetei and Jelme, contended for the first credit for having saved the boy's life,
sentences.n: Altani, Žetei, Želme γurban is 'the three: Altani, Jetei, Jelme'. köġün-ü amin aburaγsan is 'the son's life saved', with abura- 'to rescue' (stem inferred from the Ming 救) and the past participle -γsan, qualifying žuldu 'first credit' (Ming 頭功). temečeldüġešü: temeče- 'to contend' with the reciprocal -ldü- and -ġešü, the conditional -ġesü 'if, when' (Ming 呵). The conditional here is a plain 'when'.

sentences.t: Žetei, Želme qojar ügülerün:
sentences.l: Jetei, Jelme two saying:
sentences.i: Jetei and Jelme said:
sentences.n: Žetei and Želme speak, as a pair, with the same ügülerün that introduces speech throughout.

sentences.t: Man-i ügei böġesü ötör güjižü kürčü ese alaγ̇asu Altani eme küġün jakin büleġe.

morph.gloss: we, exclusive (oblique stem man-; Ming 俺) [俺行]

sentences.l: us-acc without if-be, quickly running arriving not-yet killing-if, Altani woman person how was.
sentences.i: ‘If we had not been there, and had not run up quickly and killed him, what would have become of Altani, a woman?
sentences.n: The speech of Jetei and Jelme is unmarked by Shiratori; the single quote is mine, and it closes in unit 33. Recurring grammar: the conditional -γ̇asu/-ġesü 'if' (Ming 呵) with büleġe 'was' as the answer, so that the past tense does duty for 'would have been': Man-i ügei böġesü, 'if it be without us'; ese alaγ̇asu, 'if (we) had not killed'. Man-i is 'us' with the accusative (an odd case for 'if there were no us'). eme küġün is 'woman, person' (Ming 妻 人); jakin is 'how'.

sentences.t: Köġün-ü amin-dur qor kürgekü büleġe.

morph.gloss: to bring to, cause to reach [敎到]

sentences.l: Son's life-in harm bringing was.
sentences.i: Harm would have been brought upon the boy's life.
sentences.n: qor here is 'harm, loss' (Ming 害), not the 'quiver' of the same spelling. kürgekü büleġe is the participle of kürge- 'to bring to' with büleġe 'was', here 'would have been bringing'; amin-dur is 'in the life'.

sentences.t: Žuldu man-u-γ̇ai bi-že keġebe.

morph.gloss: first credit, foremost merit (Ming 頭功) [頭功]
particle of emphasis or possession (uncertain; Ming 俺的 'ours')

sentences.l: First-credit ours is-indeed, said.
sentences.i: The first credit is ours,’ they said.
sentences.n: Žuldu man-u-γ̇ai bi-že: 'first-credit, ours, is indeed' (man-u- is the genitive of ba 'we' (exclusive; Ming 俺的); -γ̇ai is an ending I cannot account for; bi-že is bü- 'to be' with the assertion particle). keġebe is keġe- 'to say' with the past -be, 'said'. The closing single quote in `i` is mine.

sentences.t: Altani ügülerün:
sentences.l: Altani saying:
sentences.i: Altani said:
sentences.n: A short speech-introduction; the colon marks Altani's reply, which fills the next four units.

sentences.t: Min-u daγ̇un ese sonosuγ̇asu ta ker irekün büleġei.

morph.gloss: genitive: my, set after its noun
past: 'there was, used to be' (variant of -leġe)

sentences.l: My voice not-yet hearing-if, you how coming was.
sentences.i: ‘If you had not heard my voice, how would you have come?
sentences.n: Another unmarked speech; the single quote is mine. sonosuγ̇asu is sonos- 'to hear' with the conditional -uγ̇asu (Ming 聽的呵); ese 'not yet'; ker irekün büleġei, 'how (were you) coming?' (irekün, Ming 來每, with an ending -kün I cannot explain). The past büleġei again stands for 'would have'.

sentences.t: Nama-ji güjižü güjičežü šibilger in-ü barižu

morph.gloss: to overtake, catch up (stem inferred from the Ming 趕上) [趕上着]
probably a braid or lock of hair (the Ming 練︀推 gives no sense; context only; uncertain) [練︀推]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to take hold of, grasp [拿着]

sentences.l: Me running, overtaking, braid his seizing,
sentences.i: I ran, overtook him, and seized his braid,
sentences.n: Nama-ji is 'me' with the accusative -ji (oblique stem nama-); the Ming 我行 shows its 行. A subject in the accusative form is odd, and I take it as emphatic, 'as for me'. The rest repeats unit 24 in the first person; šibilger as before, 'braid' being a guess.

sentences.t: kituγai žuγuluγsan γar in-ü tatažu kituγai ese aldaγsan böġesü

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: knife drawn hand his pulling, knife not-yet slipped if-be,
sentences.i: and pulled at the hand that had drawn the knife; if the knife had not slipped from it,
sentences.n: žuγuluγsan is the past participle of žuγul- 'to draw out', 'that has drawn', qualifying γar 'hand'. aldaγsan is alda- 'to slip away' with -γsan (not the -žuγ̇ui past of unit 25); ese … böġesü is 'if it had not'. The conditional continues into the next unit.

sentences.t: Žetei, Želme qojar-i kürčü iretele köġün-ü amin-dur qor ülü-ü kürgekü büleġe. keġebe.

morph.gloss: to bring to, cause to reach [到]

sentences.l: Jetei, Jelme two-acc arriving, until-coming, son's life-in harm not-? bringing was? said.
sentences.i: before you two, Jetei and Jelme, arrived, would harm not have been brought upon the boy's life?’ she said.
sentences.n: qojar-i kürčü iretele: 'the two (accusative) arriving, until coming' (Ming 兩箇行 到着 來(間)); the accusative with kürčü is odd, and who arrives where is not clear, so `i` says only 'arrived'. ire-tele is the terminative converb, 'until'. ülü-ü is ülü 'not' with a question particle -ü (uncertain; the Ming has 麽 on the next word), so 'would harm not have been brought?', which asks for the answer 'it would have'. keġebe closes the speech; the closing quote in `i` is mine.

sentences.t: Ügülen baraγ̇asu Žuldu Altani-jin bolba.

morph.gloss: first credit, foremost merit (Ming 頭功) [頭功]
Altani, a woman's name [婦人名的]

sentences.l: Speaking when-finished, first-credit Altani's became.
sentences.i: When the speaking was ended, the first credit became Altani's.
sentences.n: Ügülen baraγ̇asu: ügüle- with the converb -n, then bara- 'to be finished' as an auxiliary with the conditional -γ̇asu, 'when the speaking was finished' (the speaker is not named; Ming 說 了呵). Žuldu Altani-jin bolba: 'first-credit Altani's became' (genitive -jin after a vowel).

sentences.t: Boroγul-un gergei Boroγul-dur nögöġe kilγun bolun Tului-jin amin-dur tusa bolba.

words.reading: 孛羅中忽勒-突︀舌兒 Boroγul-dur

sentences.l: Boroγul's wife, to-Boroγul second shaft becoming, Tului's life-in favour became.
sentences.i: Boroqul's wife became a second shaft for Boroqul, and a boon to Tolui's life.
sentences.n: nögöġe kilγun bolun, 'becoming a second shaft' (Ming 第二 轅條 'second cart-shaft'), a figure of a helper pulling beside the first; the house rendering is kept. Boroγul-dur 'to Boroqul' (dative-locative). tusa is 'favour, boon' (Ming 恩). Both bolun and bolba are bol- 'to become' (converb, past).

sentences.t: Basa Boroγul Kereid-luγ̇a Qalqalžid eled qadqulduqui-dur

morph.gloss: the Kereid, a people [種(名) 一同]

words.reading: 中合勒中合勒只惕 Qalqalžid

morph.gloss: Qalaqaljid, the name of the sands [沙磧名]

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀中灰-突︀舌兒 qadqulduqui-dur

glyphs.s: 中合惕中忽勒都︀中灰-突︀舌兒

sentences.l: Again Boroγul Kereid-with Qalqalžid sands fighting-at-the-time,
sentences.i: Again, when Boroqul fought the Kereid at Qalaqaljid-Eled,
sentences.n: Kereid-luγ̇a is the Kereid with the comitative -luγ̇a, 'with the Kereid'. Qalqalžid eled is printed in this form (`i` uses the house name Qalaqaljid-Eled, 'the Qalaqaljid Sands'); eled is el 'sand' (Ming 沙磧 'sand-waste') with the plural -d. qadqulduqui-dur is qadqul- 'to fight', reciprocal -ldu-, participle -qui, -dur, 'at the time of fighting'. Boroγul comes before the clause and also begins unit 43, so the whole is one story about him.

sentences.t: Ögödei sužiγ̇asu-ban sumun-a tusdaγ̇asu unaγ̇asu

morph.gloss: nape vein, neck pulse (Ming 頂脈; stem uncertain) [頂脈 自的行]
to be struck, hit (stem inferred from the Ming 被中) [被中呵]

sentences.l: Ögödei neck-vein-own arrow-by being-struck-if, falling-if,
sentences.i: and when Ögödei was struck by an arrow in the vein of his neck and fell,
sentences.n: sužiγ̇asu-ban is a word I cannot analyse: the Ming 頂脈 自的行 'the top-vein' (the pulse at the nape), with the reflexive -ban. sumun-a is 'by the arrow' (dative-locative, Ming 行). tusdaγ̇asu and unaγ̇asu both carry the conditional -γ̇asu (Ming 呵), 'if, when'; I read them as 'when … and when …'. Ögödei is evidently one of Chinggis's two sons (unit 46).

sentences.t: Boroγul deġere buγ̇uldužu qaγuγsan čisun in-ü ama-γ̇ar(i)-jan simižu

morph.gloss: to congeal, clot (stem inferred from the Ming 凝定) [凝定的]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to suck (stem inferred from the Ming 咂) [咂着]

sentences.l: Boroγul above dismounting-together, congealed blood his mouth-with-own sucking,
sentences.i: Boroqul got down beside him and, with his own mouth, sucked out his clotted blood,
sentences.n: deġere (Ming 上) is 'above, upon', and whether it means 'on top of him' or 'besides' is unclear, so 'beside him' is a compromise. buγ̇uldužu is buγu- 'to come down, dismount' with -ldu- 'together' and -žu (Ming 共下着). qaγuγsan čisun in-ü, 'congealed blood his' (qaγu- 'to congeal' inferred from the Ming 凝定); ama-γ̇ar(i)-jan, 'with his own mouth' (instrumental -γ̇ar, reflexive -(i)jan).

sentences.t: süni qonoldužu manaγar-ši morin-dur unuγ̇ulžu saγ̇un jadaqu-ji sundulažu

morph.gloss: to ride double (stem uncertain; Ming 疊騎 'double riding') [疊騎着]

sentences.l: night passing-together, tomorrow-toward horse-on making-ride, sitting, being-unable-acc, riding-double,
sentences.i: and passed the night together. In the morning he put him on a horse and, since he could not sit up, rode double with him,
sentences.n: qonoldužu is qono- 'to pass the night', joint -ldu-, -žu. manaγar-ši is 'tomorrow, toward' (Ming 明早). saγ̇un jadaqu-ji is 'sitting, the being unable (accusative)', which I give as 'since he could not sit up'. sundulažu (Ming 疊騎 'riding doubled') is my 'rode double'; the stem is uncertain, but the Ming suggests riding two to a horse.

sentences.t: Ogödei-jin qoināča teberižü böglegsen čisun šimin šimin

morph.gloss: to embrace (stem inferred from the Ming 抱) [抱着]
to clog, clot (stem inferred from the Ming 塞) [塞了的]

sentences.l: Ögödei's from-behind embracing, clotted blood sucking, sucking,
sentences.i: holding Ögödei from behind and sucking at the clotted blood again and again,
sentences.n: teberižü is teberi- 'to embrace' (stem inferred from the Ming 抱) with -žü. böglegsen čisun: bögle- 'to clog, clot' (the Ming 塞) with -gsen, 'blood that had clotted'. šimin šimin: šimi- 'to suck' with the converb -n, doubled for repetition, 'sucking and sucking' (Ming 咂着 咂着).

sentences.t: aman-u žabaži-jar hulaγ̇adažu Ogödei-jin amin esen kürgežü irežü büleġe.

morph.gloss: lips, edge of the mouth (Ming 口脗; stem uncertain) [口脗(行)]
to redden, be red (stem inferred from the Ming 紅) [紅着]

sentences.l: mouth's lips-with reddening, Ögödei's life safe delivering, coming was.
sentences.i: and, his mouth and lips red with blood, came bringing Ögödei with his life safe.
sentences.n: aman-u žabaži-jar is 'with the lip of the mouth' (Ming 口約 口脗行; žabaži from the Ming 口脗, stem uncertain), the instrumental -jar after a vowel. kürgežü irežü büleġe is kürge- 'to bring' + -žü, ire- 'to come' + -žü, 'bringing, coming, was', i.e. 'came bringing'. esen 'safe, whole' (Ming 安存). `i` adds 'with blood'; the Ming says only 'red'.

sentences.t: Eke-jin min-u težiġen žobaγsan hači qojar köġüd-ün min-u amin-dur tusa bolba-že.

morph.gloss: genitive: my, set after its noun
to toil, suffer (stem inferred from the Ming 生受) [生受了的]
genitive: my, set after its noun

sentences.l: Mother's my rearing toiled requital, two sons' my life-in favour became-indeed.
sentences.i: As requital for my mother's toil in rearing, they became a boon to the lives of my two sons.
sentences.n: The grammar tells the sense: min-u (post-posed 'my') belongs to the nouns before it, so Eke-jin min-u is 'of my mother' and qojar köġüd-ün min-u amin-dur is 'in the life of my two sons'. težiġen žobaγsan is 'the rearing, the having toiled' (težiġe- 'to rear'; žoba- 'to toil' from the Ming 生受). hači (Ming 還報) is 'requital', tusa 'boon'. 'They' is supplied: Altani and Boroqul, who saved Tolui and Ögödei, a reading by context. bolba-že is the past of bol- plus the assertion -že (Ming 做了 也者︀ 'done, so be it'). težiġen žobaγsan has no object in the Mongol, so `i` gives none.

sentences.t: Boroγul na-dur nököčežü darbaγ̇an urija-dāča daγ̇un demēče ese qožidaba-že.

morph.gloss: beckoning, a signal (Ming 招; stem uncertain) [招]
ablative or similar (written with a long vowel; the Ming has 行; uncertain)
to answer (stem inferred from the Ming 應) [應行]
ablative: from (written with a long vowel)
to lag behind, fall behind (stem inferred from the Ming 落後) [落後了也者︀]

sentences.l: Boroγul, me-to companion-being, beckoning, calling-from, voice answering-from, not-yet fell-behind-indeed.
sentences.i: Boroqul, as my companion, never lagged behind at the beckoning, at the calling, or at the answering of a voice.
sentences.n: The Mongol is a string of three phrases and the Ming's glosses are the main help: darbaγ̇an is 'a beckon' (Ming 招), urija-dāča 'from calling' (urija- 'to call', Ming 喚; the -dāča ending, with a long vowel, is not explained, and the Ming's 行 is its usual dative marker), daγ̇un demēče 'answering the voice' (deme- 'to answer', Ming 應). My rendering 'at the beckoning … at the answering of a voice' is a guess. qožidaba-že is qožida- 'to lag behind' (Ming 落後) with the past and the assertion -že.

sentences.t: Boroγul jesün aldal- aldaγ̇asu bu aldatuγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.

morph.gloss: fault, penalty (first half of a word broken at the line end: aldal-aldaγ̇asu) [罰]
to incur a penalty, be at fault [罰呵]
converb that closes a quotation: saying

sentences.l: Boroγul nine fault, fault-incurring-if, not let-be-penalised" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: If Boroqul incurs a penalty nine times, let him not be penalised.” So he made it a decree.
sentences.n: aldal- aldaγ̇asu is a cognate pair split by the line end: aldal 'a fault, penalty' + alda- 'to incur a penalty' with the conditional -γ̇asu (Ming 罰 罰呵), 'if he incurs a penalty'. jesün, 'nine' (Ming 九次 'nine times'): the same nine-times clause stands at §211 (for Jelme) and earlier, and as there the words do not say 'pardoned'. bu aldatuγai is the prohibitive bu with the optative -tuγai, 'let him not be penalised'. keġen žarliγ bolba is 'saying, decree he made'. The closing quotation mark of the long speech is Shiratori's, at aldatuγai.

sentences.t: "Basa ökin urug(i)-jan sojurγal öġüje" keġebe.

morph.gloss: family, kin (Ming 族; the (i) is Shiratori's) [族 自的行]

sentences.l: Again "girl kin-own-to favour let-us-give," said.
sentences.i: Again: “Let us give a favour to the girl, to her own kin,” he said.
sentences.n: A whole section in one line, and a doubtful one. ökin is 'girl, daughter' (Ming 女子), urug(i)-jan 'to her own kin' (urug 'family, kin', Ming 族, with the reflexive -(i)jan; the Ming marks it 行 'to'), sojurγal 'favour, bounty', öġüje 'let us give' (hortative -üje, Ming 與咱). The text does not say who the girl is or whether ökin is singular or plural, so `i` stays with the singular and I do not guess. Shiratori marks both quotation marks.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Usun ebügen-e ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]

sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, Usun old-man-to saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Usun-Ebügen:
sentences.n: ebügen-e is 'to the old man' (dative -e), Usun ebügen being 'Usun the old man' (house name Usun-Ebügen, as in §§208–210). The colon opens a speech that runs to unit 59, with Shiratori's opening quotation mark at Usun and the closing mark at atuγai.

sentences.t: "Usun, Qunan, Kökösös, Degei ede dörben üžegsen(i)-jen sonosuγsan(i)-jan

morph.gloss: to see [見了的 自的行]
to hear [聽了的 自的行]

sentences.l: "Usun, Qunan, Kökösös, Degei these four seen-own heard-own
sentences.i: “These four, Usun, Qunan, Kökösös and Degei, what they had seen and what they had heard,
sentences.n: ede dörben is 'these four' (Ming 這(的每) 四箇), the list before it. Usun himself is one of the four he addresses. üžegsen(i)-jen and sonosuγsan(i)-jan are the past participles of üže- 'to see' and sonos- 'to hear' with the reflexive-possessive (the (i) is Shiratori's), 'what each had seen, what each had heard' (Ming 見了的 自的行, 聽了的 自的行). A recurring pattern: -(i)jen/-(i)jan, back and front vowel forms. The unit runs on into the next.

sentences.t: ülü niγ̇un qabčin žiγ̇an aqun büleġei.

morph.gloss: hiding, concealment (Ming 匿; stem uncertain; relation to the qabči- 'clamp' of qabčižu unclear) [匿]
past: 'there was, used to be' (variant of -leġe)

sentences.l: not hiding, concealing, telling being was.
sentences.i: they told me without hiding or concealing.
sentences.n: ülü niγ̇un qabčin is 'not hiding, concealing', ülü being the plain negative before the converb niγ̇un (niγu- 'to hide'); qabčin (Ming 匿) is probably a second verb or noun for concealing, and whether it is related to the qabči- 'clamp' of unit 19 I cannot say. žiγ̇an aqun büleġei is 'telling, being, was'; aqun is an ending I cannot explain (the Ming gives 有 'be'). 'Me' in `i` is supplied.

sentences.t: Uqaγsan sedkigsen(i)-jen kelelen aqun büleġei.

morph.gloss: to think [想了的 自的行]
past: 'there was, used to be' (variant of -leġe)

sentences.l: What-was-understood, what-thought-own speaking being was.
sentences.i: They spoke out what they had understood and what they had thought.
sentences.n: Uqaγsan is the participle of uqa- 'to understand' (Ming 省了的); sedkigsen(i)-jen 'what one has thought' (sedki- 'to think', with the reflexive; Ming 想了的 自的行); kelelen 'speaking' (kele-, converb -n). aqun büleġei as in the previous unit.

sentences.t: Moṅγol-un töre nojan mör beki bolqui josun ažuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: the Mongols (the Ming glosses 達達 'Tatars') [達達的]
beki, a title of rank [官名]

sentences.l: Mongols' rule, lords' way, beki becoming custom was.
sentences.i: It was the Mongols' custom, the way of the lords, that one become beki.
sentences.n: Moṅγol-un töre is 'of the Mongols, the rule' (the Ming glosses Moṅγol as 達達 'Tatars'; töre 'rule, principle', Ming 理). nojan mör, 'the lords' way/trail' (Ming 官 道子); beki bolqui josun, 'beki becoming custom', with the participle bolqui. The readings of töre and mör here are both loose, and `i` follows the sense of the whole line. ažuγ̇ui is 'was' with the past -žuγ̇ui, as in unit 25.

sentences.t: Baγ̇arin aqa-jin uruγ büleġei.

morph.gloss: past: 'there was, used to be' (variant of -leġe)

sentences.l: Baγ̇arin elder's offspring was.
sentences.i: It was the descendants of the elder of the Ba'arin.
sentences.n: Baγ̇arin aqa-jin uruγ büleġei, 'of the Ba'arin, the elder's, descendants were'. aqa-jin is 'of the elder' (genitive after a vowel; Ming 長的). I read this clause as completing the last: the beki had been taken from the senior line of the Ba'arin. No verb of 'taking' stands in the text, so it is an inference.

sentences.t: Beki mör bidan-u dotora deġere-eče beki Usun ebügen boltuγai.

morph.gloss: beki, a title of rank [官名]
beki, a title of rank [官名]

sentences.l: Beki way us-of among above-from, beki Usun old-man let-be.
sentences.i: As for the way of beki, from among us, from the top, let Usun-Ebügen be beki.
sentences.n: mör, Ming 道子, is the 'way' of the previous unit, here again 'way', now the beki's way (a loose reading). bidan-u dotora is 'of us, among' (bidan-u is the inclusive 'we', Ming 咱的); deġere-eče 'from above' (Ming 自 上), which I take as 'from the top' of the company, i.e. first. boltuγai is the optative 'let him be' (Ming 做者︀). beki is a title of rank (Ming 官名).

sentences.t: Beki ergüġed čaγaγ̇an deġel emüsčü čaγan aγta unuγ̇ulžu saγ̇uri deġere saγ̇ulžu takižu

morph.gloss: beki, a title of rank [官名]
seat, place of sitting, rank in sitting [坐位]
to serve, wait on (stem inferred from the Ming 侍奉) [侍奉着]

sentences.l: Beki raising, white robe wearing, white gelding making-ride, seat above making-sit, serving
sentences.i: Raise the beki up, let him wear a white robe, set him on a white gelding, seat him on the seat, and serve him,
sentences.n: A chain of converbs, with the main verb in the next unit's closing words. ergüġed (ergü- 'to lift, raise', Ming 擡了 'raised'), emüsčü ('wearing', emüs-; it is not causative, so the beki himself is the wearer and `i` says 'let him wear'), unuγ̇ulžu ('making ride', causative of unu- 'to ride'), saγ̇ulžu ('seating', causative of saγ̇u-), takižu ('serving', taki- inferred from the Ming 侍奉). Ming 白 騸馬 is 'white gelding'. 'saγ̇uri deġere' is 'upon the seat' (saγ̇uri 'seat, rank in sitting', Ming 坐位).

sentences.t: basa hon sara satažu tein atuγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.

morph.gloss: to deliberate, discuss (stem uncertain; Ming 議論) [議論着]
converb that closes a quotation: saying

sentences.l: Again year, month deliberating, so let-it-be" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: and again deliberate the years and the months; let it be so,” he said, and made it a decree.
sentences.n: hon sara satažu is 'year, month, reckoning', with satažu from sata- (stem uncertain; Ming 論着 'discussing'). satažu continues the converb chain of the unit before it, so those who serve the beki are the ones who deliberate; whether they do so with him, or whether he is the one who settles the years and months, the words do not say (the Ming 議論 'deliberate' is as far as I can go). tein atuγai is 'so let it be' (atuγai is a- 'to be' with the optative -tuγai). The closing quotation mark of the speech is Shiratori's, at atuγai; keġen žarliγ bolba as in unit 49.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: The introduction of the last speech of the part; Shiratori's opening quotation mark is at Quildar in the next unit and the closing mark at atuγai.

sentences.t: "Quildar anda qadqulduγ̇an-dur ami-jan örežü

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀安-突︀舌兒 qadqulduγ̇an-dur

glyphs.s: 中合惕中忽勒都︀安-突︀舌兒

morph.gloss: to put forth, stake (stem inferred; Ming 出着 'put out') [出着]

sentences.l: "Quildar sworn-brother fighting-in life-own putting-forth,
sentences.i: “Quildar, the sworn brother, in battle risking his own life,
sentences.n: anda is 'sworn brother' (Ming 契交). qadqulduγ̇an-dur is qadqu- 'to fight', the reciprocal -ldu-, the noun-maker -γ̇an 'a fighting', and -dur, 'in the battle' (Ming 厮殺︀ 時 'at the time of fighting'). ami-jan is 'his own life' (ami with the reflexive -jan, Ming 性命自的行). örežü is öre- 'to put forth, stake' (Ming 出着 'putting out'; the same word and Ming as in ami-jan öregsen-ü tula, §§208–210), so `i` says 'risking his own life'. Quildar is presumably the Mongqud Quildar(-Sečen) of §§170–185, also called anda in §§208–210; the decree for his line that follows repeats the one at the end of §§182–185.

sentences.t: urida aman neġegsen-(n)ü tusa-jin tula

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's)
because of, on account of [上頭]

sentences.l: formerly mouth opened-of favour-of on-account,
sentences.i: because of the service of having been first to open his mouth,
sentences.n: urida is 'formerly, first' (Ming 先). aman neġegsen-(n)ü is 'of the mouth that has opened' (aman 'mouth', Ming 口; neġe- 'to open', participle -gsen, genitive -(n)ü), and tusa-jin tula 'on account of the favour' (tula 'because of', Ming 上頭). What 'opening the mouth' means (speaking up first, volunteering, giving the first word) the text does not say, and `i` leaves the phrase literal.

sentences.t: uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele önöčid-ün abliγa abun atuγai"

morph.gloss: solitary one, forlorn (Ming 孤獨; stem uncertain) [孤獨(每)的]
a grant received (Ming 受賜 'receive a grant'; sense uncertain) [受賜]

sentences.l: offspring's offspring-to until forlorn's grant taking let-be"
sentences.i: down to the offspring of his offspring, let them receive the grant of the forlorn.”
sentences.n: uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele: 'offspring's offspring-to, until' (kürtele is kür- 'to reach' with the terminative -tele, 'down to'; Ming 子孫的 子孫行 直到). önöčid-ün abliγa abun atuγai: 'of the forlorn, grant, taking, let it be'. önöčid is 'solitary ones' (Ming 孤獨每) and abliγa is Ming 受賜 'receive a grant' (at §§182–185 the same word has the Ming 請受 'request and receive'), so the sense is a grant for orphans or the solitary, but the exact meaning is uncertain. 'Let them receive' supplies the subject. The closing quotation mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.

morph.gloss: converb that closes a quotation: saying

sentences.l: saying decree made.
sentences.i: So he made it a decree.
sentences.n: keġen žarliγ bolba, the formula of closing as at the end of §214 and §216 (keġe-, converb -n, 'saying'; žarliγ 'decree', Ming 聖旨; bolba 'made').
